text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The ruling Socialist party caved in to opposition demands, returning its mandate to form a second government and agreeing to early parliamentary elections.
-- Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov said on Tuesday he would call early polls in April and he would appoint a caretaker cabinet in a week. @
-- Bulgaria's opposition appealed to all protesters to lift baricades and roadblocks in the country after the ruling Socialists agreed to opposition demands for early elections.
-- Thousands of Bulgarians poured in the streets of Sofia to celebrate with songs and dances the ruling Socialists' decision to step down from power.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank foreign exchange reserves fell to $415 million on January 31 from $518 million a month earlier because of a $135.1 million coupon payment on Brady bonds on January 28.
-- The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) which manages state equity in local commercial banks posted 749 million levs loss in 1996, BCC executive director Valentin Tzvetanov said.
-- The ruling Socialist party (BSP) leader Georgi Parvanov said he would ask for a confidence vote from the party's Supreme Council after the party gave up forming a new government.
-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim said it could stop work today because of shortage of crude and finances. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
